Seminar Title:

A Novel Routing Strategy and Capacity Planning in QKD-Enabled Optical Networks

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Arup Kumar Marik ( Rollno : 524ec1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC Seminar Room (EC-303 )

Date and Time:

14 Oct 2026 5.30 P.M

Contact:

Sadananda Behera

Abstract:

Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) provides information-theoretic security. However, practical deployment of QKD-enabled optical networks is constrained by transmission-distance limitations, which lead to low Secure Key Rates (SKRs) and thereby limited secret-key resources. Consequently, increasing traffic demand can cause rapid key depletion on heavily utilized links and degrade secure service provisioning. This work develops a resource-aware framework that jointly addresses connection ordering, secret-key-aware routing, and selective capacity enhancement. A Path Diversity-based connection ordering strategy is proposed to account for differences in key-depletion costs among alternative paths. Furthermore, a Least Key Depletion (LKD) routing strategy is developed to select paths by minimizing the maximum key-depletion ratio across their constituent links. To alleviate persistent key bottlenecks, a Key Utilization Factor (KUF) is introduced to identify links requiring selective parallel QKD deployment. The proposed framework is evaluated on a 28-node reference metro optical network using a distance-dependent SKR model and the Security Probability (SP) and Key Demand Success Ratio (KDSR) as performance metrics. Results show that Path Diversity Ascending provides a favorable balance between SP, KDSR, and key blocking, while LKD consistently outperforms conventional Shortest Path First (SPF) routing in both SP and KDSR. For capacity enhancement, KUF achieves SP&gt=0.99&nbspwith only 6 upgraded links, compared with 36 links required by Edge Betweenness Centrality (EBC). Upgrading these six links requires 12 additional QKD modules and maintains SP&gt=0.99 over the considered traffic range. These results demonstrate that jointly optimizing connection ordering, key-aware routing, and selective capacity enhancement can improve secret-key utilization and provide an efficient approach to scalable QKD network capacity planning.
